newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal June CPI may revive rate cut expectations.
newsitem.headline: Portugal June CPI may revive rate cut expectations.

text.p: Portugal's year-on-year inflation rate for June may drop below two percent, leading to revived expectations of a cut in Bank of Portugal (BP) rates, Banco Cisf said on Wednesday.

"This situation (inflation below two percent) will tend to revive expectations of a rate cut after release of the consumer price index (CPI), if debate on German and French budget measures does not generate market volatility", it said in a weekly report.
"The June year-on-year inflation rate may drop below two percent, confirming the reversal of significant rises by some food goods in the previous month", it added.
In May prices rose by 0.7 percent month-on-month, for a rolling average rate over the past 12 months of 3.0 percent and a year-on-year rate of 2.1 percent.
The National Statistics Institue will release the June figures by July 14.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a June monthly price change of between a negative 0.1 to a rise of 0.3 percent, with a year-on-year rate of between 2.0 percent and 2.4 percent.
In either case the rolling 12-month average would be 2.9 percent.
